1	Reviewer: codex-gpt-6
2	Date: 2026-09-28
3	Scope: targeted C12 workspace-model reuse review; plan and implementation, read-only
4	Plan: /home/research/work/plans/local-llm-multiarch-plan.md
5	Plan SHA256: 714b391ffb76237fcb7db79d13051c0c7869e0cd9714770c98be992391bb6be4
6	Plan modified: 2026-09-28 19:56:51.300109126 +0200
7	Implementation: /home/research/dev/local-llms, branch local-llm-multiarch
8	Reviewed HEAD: d3c6a94aa12ea100ac936248f40f9c6fe3a51b95
9	C12 baseline: 8af8ae8e7c324dfdf48d12ff5333d5be8c8468dc
10	Worktree: clean at the start and on repeated checks through report preparation
11	C12 binary diff SHA256: 08577763e16d6a2df74abe4c804908274dc4bb4d17106159200b27ae9ac34d3c
12	
13	## Verdict
14	
15	C12 has the right intended scope and works for an ordinary, stable GGUF file in the shared directory, but **this implementation is not ready for acceptance**. I confirmed six major defects involving verification, symlinks, fresh HF snapshots, disk admission, resumable partials and copy handling, plus two minor reporting/accounting defects. The existing targeted tests all pass because they primarily exercise downloader-level happy paths, rather than the complete controller and multi-file lifecycle. Fix R1–R6 before relying on this for candidate acceptance. No backward-compatibility requirement was applied.
16	
17	I reviewed the actual development checkout, its CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, DS006, the specification matrix, current DS002 and related lifecycle/security code, C12 and §9 decisions 6–7, and the implementation log. The C12 change was already committed and clean when I began. I tested a 1.1 MB `git archive` snapshot of that exact commit at `/tmp/c12-review-ywenp317`; none of the developer's source files were edited. The plan hash and HEAD stayed unchanged during the review.
18	
19	**Host isolation:** no GPU use, builds, package/model downloads, container operations, or access to real model contents. The reproduction payload is 262,151 bytes. All test-created model-shaped files lived in disposable `/tmp/c12-fixture-*` directories and were removed by their fixtures. Existing downloaded models were neither read nor deleted.
20	
21	## Confirmed findings
22	
23	### R1 — Major: bytes changed during verification can be recorded as permanently trusted
24	
25	**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:399](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:399), publication at 404–410, `recordStat` at 416–420, and the reuse fast path at 825–834.
26	
27	The hash is calculated first, but the trusted device/inode/size/mtime/ctime is sampled later. There is no before/after identity check around hashing, and no association with a held descriptor for the file that was actually hashed. A shared writer can alter bytes already read by the hash; the code then records the **changed** file's metadata alongside the **old** successful digest. Future runs see matching metadata and skip hashing indefinitely.
28	
29	**Reproduction:** put the pinned 262,151-byte fixture in the shared directory. In the existing `onProgress` test seam, after the final hashing chunk, overwrite its first byte without changing its size. This simulates a writer running between the hash and final publication. Adoption returns `status: complete`, the actual file's SHA256 is wrong, and a second call returns complete with `reverified` absent and zero downloads. This is more than the unavoidable instant between a final check and opening a model: the corrupted state becomes the persistent trusted baseline.
30	
31	**Impact:** the asserted pinned identity can be false on this and every later Run, defeating C12's reason for revalidation.
32	
33	**Remediation:** bind verification to a regular-file descriptor and verify stable identity/size/timestamps before and after reading. Reject or retry on changes; do not stamp an arbitrary later path state as the state just hashed. Account explicitly for the ctime change caused by the implementation's own rename. Apply the same rule to revalidation and downloaded-file finalization, since all use `recordStat`. Add the deterministic during-hash and publication-window races to tests. For protection against writers after verification, also resolve the trust/snapshot question under “Design boundaries” below.
34	
35	### R2 — Major: symlinks can bypass confinement and defeat subsequent revalidation
36	
37	**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:292](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:292) uses `stat`, following symlinks; 315–317 records `lstat` values without requiring a regular file; 823–834 hashes through the path and then caches those values. Shared traversal at 339–351 trusts directory entries across later pathname operations.
38	
39	Two isolated reproductions confirm distinct paths through this problem:
40	
41	1. Adopt a correct file, replace the agent-store pathname with a symlink to a correct file outside the allowed model roots, then run again. It is rehashed and accepted while remaining a symlink. Modify the target, retaining its length. The next call trusts the **unchanged symlink's** stat and returns corrupted bytes without revalidation.
42	2. Return a directory entry from `readdir`, then replace that directory with a symlink before recursion. The walker follows it, adopts a correctly hashed file outside the shared root and reports success. The current test with symlinks already present before enumeration does not cover this.
43	
44	**Impact:** the plan's “regular files only; no symlinks; nothing outside those roots” rule is not implemented for the agent store or concurrent traversal. Even benign link substitution can disable the intended changed-file check.
45	
46	**Remediation:** require regular files throughout both lookup paths. Open and validate candidates without following links and keep verification/adoption bound to that opened object. Protect resolution of ancestor directories as well as the final component; checking only `lstat` of the leaf is insufficient. Do not use a symlink inode's stat to authenticate its target. Add own-store symlinks, ancestor swaps and copy-fallback swaps to the negative tests.
47	
48	### R3 — Major: adopting the first file of a new HF snapshot fails with ENOENT
49	
50	**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:380](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:380) creates only the partial's parent; rename at 409 targets `paths.file`. [snapshotFilePaths:993](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:993) deliberately places partials under `hf/.state/<repo>/<commit>` and final files under `hf/<repo>/<commit>`. Creation of the latter at 848 occurs only after the adoption branch has returned.
51	
52	**Reproduction:** use an empty HF store and place a correct pinned `config.json` fixture in the shared directory. Call `downloadSnapshotFile` with `adoptFrom`. Hash verification succeeds, then rename fails:
53	
54	```text
55	ENOENT: rename '.../hf/.state/org/model/<commit>/config.json.partial'
56	            -> '.../hf/org/model/<commit>/config.json'
57	```
58	
59	**Impact:** the stated snapshot reuse feature fails on its natural first-use case, despite a fully available matching file. A snapshot whose final directory already exists happens to avoid the failure.
60	
61	**Remediation:** securely create both destination and staging parents before adoption, without weakening R2's confinement checks. Test a complete fresh snapshot with both git-oid metadata files and SHA256/LFS weights, a partially present snapshot, and mixed adopted/downloaded files. Do not pre-create the final directory in the principal acceptance test.
62	
63	### R4 — Major: Run requires full download space before discovering reusable hard links
64	
65	**Evidence:** [deployments.mjs:1039](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/deployments.mjs:1039) computes remaining bytes from `weightsState` and refuses admission at 1044–1045; shared discovery is reached only in the later `store.fetch`. Preview and overview make the same assumption at 419–426 and 472–485. The store's state functions inspect only canonical local paths, not shared candidates.
66	
67	**Reproduction:** put a matching fixture in the shared directory on the same mount as the store. Give the real controller otherwise ample GPU/RAM and a disk snapshot with half the fixture size free. The actual `controller.run` returns `admission_insufficient_now`; the download/adoption function is called zero times. A hard link plus small bookkeeping would fit, but the feature is never attempted.
68	
69	**Impact:** reuse is refused in precisely the low-disk situation where avoiding a second model allocation matters. The UI can refuse Run before the user can obtain the benefit. Successful direct `downloadArtifact` tests miss this integration failure.
70	
71	**Remediation:** plan artifact acquisition before making the disk part of admission final: distinguish already-owned files, verified linkable candidates, files requiring copies, and missing bytes requiring downloads. Keep normal hardware/memory refusal before expensive acquisition. Revalidate candidates before use and check space for the actual copy/download/staging requirement, not blindly zero or the entire model. Make Run and its previews agree, and add a real-controller low-disk reuse test. See the mount caveat below: do not assume every shared candidate is linkable.
72	
73	### R5 — Major: trying a wrong shared candidate destroys an existing resumable download
74	
75	**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:379](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:379) calls `removePartial` before a candidate has been hashed; the candidate then occupies the normal `.partial` pathname. Hash mismatch at 400–402 removes it again, and fallback resumes from the now-empty store.
76	
77	**Reproduction:** create a correct 131,072-byte prefix and matching identity sidecar for the 262,151-byte artifact. Place a same-sized, wrong-hash file in the shared directory. Invoke download. The first mocked HTTP request has **no Range header**: the valid prefix was deleted. A valid candidate whose adoption is cancelled can similarly displace valuable progress.
78	
79	**Impact:** merely having an unrelated same-sized model in the shared directory causes an unnecessary full re-download, directly undermining the feature's purpose and existing resume contract. With real models this can discard gigabytes of valid progress.
80	
81	**Remediation:** use an independent, unique adoption staging path. Retain the previous partial and its identity until a fully verified replacement is ready to publish. On a mismatch, copy/link failure or cancellation, discard only that candidate's staging file and resume the original prefix. Test the Range offset after all these outcomes.
82	
83	### R6 — Major: copy fallback bypasses disk protection and cannot be promptly cancelled
84	
85	**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:382](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:382) falls back from every link exception to one awaited `copyFile`; that call has no cancellation or progress mechanism, performs no free-space check, and swallows all copy errors. `assertFreeSpace` is only reached at 847 after adoption has failed. [deployments.mjs:979](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/deployments.mjs:979) aborts and then awaits the same job, so Stop/Cancel cannot complete while copying is outstanding.
86	
87	**Reproductions:**
88	
89	- Force link to return EXDEV and inject a `statfs` result of zero available bytes. Adoption returns a successful copy and the space-check seam is called **zero times**. Only the tiny fixture was actually copied; this was not a disk-filling experiment.
90	- Hold the copy operation on a test promise, abort the signal, and observe that the operation remains unsettled. It ends with `ABORTED` only after the copy is released. No real slow/large file was needed.
91	
92	**Impact:** a copy can consume the space that the download path would preserve and can hold controller Stop/Cancel/drain through a long I/O operation. A copy-space or permission failure is hidden as a candidate miss and may trigger an unnecessary network attempt.
93	
94	**Remediation:** identify expected link-fallback errors, revalidate the source, and preflight the copy's actual space requirement and reserve. Copy in abortable bounded chunks (or use a managed, cancellable helper), report copying/verifying progress and clean only its own staging file. Propagate meaningful ENOSPC, cancellation and filesystem errors rather than silently treating them as a nonexistent model. Test these paths with injected faults; no large production model is needed.
95	
96	### R7 — Minor: adoption provenance is missing or printed as undefined
97	
98	**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:411](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:411) returns `{source, method}`; [weightStores.mjs:103](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/weightStores.mjs:103) preserves that field; [deployments.mjs:869](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/deployments.mjs:869) prints `entry.from`. The HF store ignores `result.adopted` entirely and returns no provenance at 267–287.
99	
100	**Reproduction:** real GGUF store adoption formats the controller message as `adopted model.gguf from undefined (link, verified)`. Pre-create a snapshot directory to get past R3, successfully adopt its fixture and inspect the returned object: `bytesTransferred: 0`, `adopted: undefined`.
101	
102	**Impact:** DS002's promise that the deployment log names every adopted file and method is false, and acceptance evidence cannot reliably show which workspace files were reused.
103	
104	**Remediation:** use one provenance shape throughout, aggregate it for every snapshot file and split shard, and test the controller's actual log output, including mixed adoption/download. Make verification a visible phase during hashing; current adoption reports ordinary download progress until the final byte and never reports copy progress.
105	
106	### R8 — Minor: snapshot deletion can report zero although it removes the inode's last links
107	
108	**Evidence:** [weightStores.mjs:229](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/weightStores.mjs:229) sums only files whose current `nlink <= 1`, **before** recursively removing the whole snapshot at 293–295.
109	
110	**Reproduction:** make two files inside one test snapshot hard links to the same 262,151-byte inode, with no external link. Delete that snapshot through its real store API. Both links are removed, yet `freedBytes` is zero. This topology can arise if identical pinned files were adopted from one shared inode and the operator later removed the shared pathname.
111	
112	**Impact:** disk accounting understates freed content when all remaining links lie inside the deletion set. The new GGUF per-file removal does not have this particular pre-scan problem.
113	
114	**Remediation:** count distinct `(device,inode)` identities and how many links the deletion set removes, or account during sequential unlinking. Do not count an inode while an external link remains. Decide whether `freedBytes` means logical content bytes or physical reclaimed blocks; the current use of `size` cannot promise exact physical space for sparse/reflinked files or files held open. Add both retained-external-link and last-internal-links tests.
115	
116	## Design boundaries and plan/spec mismatches
117	
118	These are not additional confirmed defects in the eight-item count:
119	
120	- **Same filesystem is insufficient for a hard link in the container.** C12 says same filesystem → link. Linux returns EXDEV across different mounts even if they expose the same filesystem ([Linux link(2), EXDEV](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/link.2.html)). Ploinky separately binds the shared directory to `/shared`, while this agent declares its model store under `/data`. Therefore the normal deployed path may take the copy fallback even when a host-side operator could hard-link those same files. This is an inference from the mounts, not a container experiment. Correct the wording to “when link succeeds,” and measure link-versus-copy and peak disk in the authorized nested acceptance fixture. No Ploinky architectural change is needed merely to avoid a network download.
121	- **The model store is writable shared state, not immutable evidence.** R1 fixes a concrete verification bug, but stat polling cannot prevent an external write immediately after verification or while a runner reads an adopted hard link. Define whether writers are cooperative and must not alter in-use models. If the requirement is immutable bytes against concurrent writers, use an isolated verified copy/reflink or a stronger storage/snapshot mechanism; hard-linking and checking timestamps cannot provide that guarantee. Likewise, sidecar metadata stored under workspace-writable `/data` is a cache, not authentication against a writer who can also forge that metadata. Recheck the whole artifact at the last practical point before loading, especially after fetching multiple files or preparing an on-demand runner.
122	- **The implementation does not search the whole workspace or even every file in its own store.** It trusts only the canonical own-store path with matching verification sidecar; arbitrary-name discovery is limited to `/shared/models`. A fixture already placed at the exact canonical own-store path, with correct bytes but no sidecar, was downloaded again. DS002 explicitly narrows own-store reuse this way, so I report this as a scope/design limitation rather than a backward-compatibility defect. Consider hashing/adopting an unrecorded canonical file before downloading, and document that existing benchmark/download directories require an operator placement step. Do not move or delete the real measured files during that step without the owner's approval.
123	- **Snapshot digests differ from the plan's literal SHA256 wording.** C12 promises size+SHA256 for every snapshot file; DS002 and the code retain git-blob SHA1 for small Git-backed files. The fresh-snapshot fixture above used SHA256, so R3 is independent of this mismatch. Either explicitly allow the established pinned git-oid form in the plan or implement its literal SHA256 requirement. No migration requirement follows from that choice.
124	- **Lookup is bounded by entry count, not work or I/O volume.** Each shard/snapshot file walks the tree again and can hash many same-sized candidates. The scan has no signal checks, and each `readdir` materializes the whole directory before the 20,000-entry cap is applied. A large cache should use a cancellable streaming walk or an advisory size/hash index whose candidates are still verified. This is an unmeasured scaling concern, not a claim that this review observed a large-cache failure.
125	- **The owner's model-retention instruction remains in force.** Product tests may remove their disposable fixtures; engineering must keep the real downloaded models. None of these findings calls for deleting a real model or reclaiming disk as a workaround.
126	
127	## Verification and missing tests
128	
129	From the immutable snapshot I ran:
130	
131	```sh
132	node --test local-llm/tests/shared-models.test.mjs \
133	  local-llm/tests/downloader.test.mjs \
134	  local-llm/tests/hf-snapshot.test.mjs \
135	  local-llm/tests/split-gguf.test.mjs \
136	  local-llm/tests/controller.test.mjs
137	```
138	
139	**Result: 71 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.** The implementation log's full-suite `301/301` is a reported engineering result; I did not independently rerun the whole suite. The six new tests in `shared-models.test.mjs` use single GGUF files and do not cover a real controller Run, a fresh adopted HF snapshot, or split-file adoption. Their static symlink and between-call mutation fixtures do not cover R1/R2. The old-record test is permissible, but preserving old record behavior is not an acceptance requirement.
140	
141	The additional isolated script below ran successfully and confirmed 12 observations: R1; both R2 paths; R3; R4; R5; both R6 paths; both R7 paths; R8; and the unrecorded-own-file design limitation. Test hooks only schedule races, simulate EXDEV/space and hold a copy; they do not alter the reviewed implementation. No GPU or network is used.
142	
143	After fixes, add the above regression cases and an end-to-end **small fixture** matrix: complete, incomplete, corrupt and mixed-source split GGUF/HF snapshots; completion only after every required file verifies; partial preservation; Stop/Cancel/drain; actual provenance; and inode-aware deletion. Then the authorized Spark acceptance can prove model reuse with the already-retained pinned weights. Correct bytes and zero network transfer must be demonstrated independently from runner performance.
144	
145	## Reproduction appendix
146	
147	The preserved script is also at `/tmp/c12-review-ywenp317/reproduce_codex.mjs`. To reproduce against the exact commit in a separate small source copy:
148	
149	```sh
150	snapshot_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/c12-review-repeat-XXXXXX)
151	git -C /home/research/dev/local-llms archive d3c6a94aa12ea100ac936248f40f9c6fe3a51b95 | tar -x -C "$snapshot_dir"
152	# Save the JavaScript below as "$snapshot_dir/reproduce_codex.mjs".
153	node "$snapshot_dir/reproduce_codex.mjs"
154	```
155	
156	The script removes only directories it itself creates with the `c12-fixture-` prefix. It does not read existing model paths. Its assertions describe the observed defects, so a successful fix should make the corresponding assertion fail; convert them to desired-behavior regression assertions when adding repository tests.

160	import os from 'node:os';
161	import path from 'node:path';

## Verdict

C12 has the right intended scope and works for an ordinary, stable GGUF file in the shared directory, but **this implementation is not ready for acceptance**. I confirmed six major defects involving verification, symlinks, fresh HF snapshots, disk admission, resumable partials and copy handling, plus two minor reporting/accounting defects. The existing targeted tests all pass because they primarily exercise downloader-level happy paths, rather than the complete controller and multi-file lifecycle. Fix R1–R6 before relying on this for candidate acceptance. No backward-compatibility requirement was applied.

I reviewed the actual development checkout, its CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, DS006, the specification matrix, current DS002 and related lifecycle/security code, C12 and §9 decisions 6–7, and the implementation log. The C12 change was already committed and clean when I began. I tested a 1.1 MB `git archive` snapshot of that exact commit at `/tmp/c12-review-ywenp317`; none of the developer's source files were edited. The plan hash and HEAD stayed unchanged during the review.

**Host isolation:** no GPU use, builds, package/model downloads, container operations, or access to real model contents. The reproduction payload is 262,151 bytes. All test-created model-shaped files lived in disposable `/tmp/c12-fixture-*` directories and were removed by their fixtures. Existing downloaded models were neither read nor deleted.

## Confirmed findings

### R1 — Major: bytes changed during verification can be recorded as permanently trusted

**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:399](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:399), publication at 404–410, `recordStat` at 416–420, and the reuse fast path at 825–834.

The hash is calculated first, but the trusted device/inode/size/mtime/ctime is sampled later. There is no before/after identity check around hashing, and no association with a held descriptor for the file that was actually hashed. A shared writer can alter bytes already read by the hash; the code then records the **changed** file's metadata alongside the **old** successful digest. Future runs see matching metadata and skip hashing indefinitely.

**Reproduction:** put the pinned 262,151-byte fixture in the shared directory. In the existing `onProgress` test seam, after the final hashing chunk, overwrite its first byte without changing its size. This simulates a writer running between the hash and final publication. Adoption returns `status: complete`, the actual file's SHA256 is wrong, and a second call returns complete with `reverified` absent and zero downloads. This is more than the unavoidable instant between a final check and opening a model: the corrupted state becomes the persistent trusted baseline.

**Impact:** the asserted pinned identity can be false on this and every later Run, defeating C12's reason for revalidation.

**Remediation:** bind verification to a regular-file descriptor and verify stable identity/size/timestamps before and after reading. Reject or retry on changes; do not stamp an arbitrary later path state as the state just hashed. Account explicitly for the ctime change caused by the implementation's own rename. Apply the same rule to revalidation and downloaded-file finalization, since all use `recordStat`. Add the deterministic during-hash and publication-window races to tests. For protection against writers after verification, also resolve the trust/snapshot question under “Design boundaries” below.

### R2 — Major: symlinks can bypass confinement and defeat subsequent revalidation

**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:292](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:292) uses `stat`, following symlinks; 315–317 records `lstat` values without requiring a regular file; 823–834 hashes through the path and then caches those values. Shared traversal at 339–351 trusts directory entries across later pathname operations.

Two isolated reproductions confirm distinct paths through this problem:

1. Adopt a correct file, replace the agent-store pathname with a symlink to a correct file outside the allowed model roots, then run again. It is rehashed and accepted while remaining a symlink. Modify the target, retaining its length. The next call trusts the **unchanged symlink's** stat and returns corrupted bytes without revalidation.
2. Return a directory entry from `readdir`, then replace that directory with a symlink before recursion. The walker follows it, adopts a correctly hashed file outside the shared root and reports success. The current test with symlinks already present before enumeration does not cover this.

**Impact:** the plan's “regular files only; no symlinks; nothing outside those roots” rule is not implemented for the agent store or concurrent traversal. Even benign link substitution can disable the intended changed-file check.

**Remediation:** require regular files throughout both lookup paths. Open and validate candidates without following links and keep verification/adoption bound to that opened object. Protect resolution of ancestor directories as well as the final component; checking only `lstat` of the leaf is insufficient. Do not use a symlink inode's stat to authenticate its target. Add own-store symlinks, ancestor swaps and copy-fallback swaps to the negative tests.

### R3 — Major: adopting the first file of a new HF snapshot fails with ENOENT

**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:380](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:380) creates only the partial's parent; rename at 409 targets `paths.file`. [snapshotFilePaths:993](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:993) deliberately places partials under `hf/.state/<repo>/<commit>` and final files under `hf/<repo>/<commit>`. Creation of the latter at 848 occurs only after the adoption branch has returned.

**Reproduction:** use an empty HF store and place a correct pinned `config.json` fixture in the shared directory. Call `downloadSnapshotFile` with `adoptFrom`. Hash verification succeeds, then rename fails:

```text
ENOENT: rename '.../hf/.state/org/model/<commit>/config.json.partial'
            -> '.../hf/org/model/<commit>/config.json'
```

**Impact:** the stated snapshot reuse feature fails on its natural first-use case, despite a fully available matching file. A snapshot whose final directory already exists happens to avoid the failure.

**Remediation:** securely create both destination and staging parents before adoption, without weakening R2's confinement checks. Test a complete fresh snapshot with both git-oid metadata files and SHA256/LFS weights, a partially present snapshot, and mixed adopted/downloaded files. Do not pre-create the final directory in the principal acceptance test.

### R4 — Major: Run requires full download space before discovering reusable hard links

**Evidence:** [deployments.mjs:1039](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/deployments.mjs:1039) computes remaining bytes from `weightsState` and refuses admission at 1044–1045; shared discovery is reached only in the later `store.fetch`. Preview and overview make the same assumption at 419–426 and 472–485. The store's state functions inspect only canonical local paths, not shared candidates.

**Reproduction:** put a matching fixture in the shared directory on the same mount as the store. Give the real controller otherwise ample GPU/RAM and a disk snapshot with half the fixture size free. The actual `controller.run` returns `admission_insufficient_now`; the download/adoption function is called zero times. A hard link plus small bookkeeping would fit, but the feature is never attempted.

**Impact:** reuse is refused in precisely the low-disk situation where avoiding a second model allocation matters. The UI can refuse Run before the user can obtain the benefit. Successful direct `downloadArtifact` tests miss this integration failure.

**Remediation:** plan artifact acquisition before making the disk part of admission final: distinguish already-owned files, verified linkable candidates, files requiring copies, and missing bytes requiring downloads. Keep normal hardware/memory refusal before expensive acquisition. Revalidate candidates before use and check space for the actual copy/download/staging requirement, not blindly zero or the entire model. Make Run and its previews agree, and add a real-controller low-disk reuse test. See the mount caveat below: do not assume every shared candidate is linkable.

### R5 — Major: trying a wrong shared candidate destroys an existing resumable download

**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:379](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:379) calls `removePartial` before a candidate has been hashed; the candidate then occupies the normal `.partial` pathname. Hash mismatch at 400–402 removes it again, and fallback resumes from the now-empty store.

**Reproduction:** create a correct 131,072-byte prefix and matching identity sidecar for the 262,151-byte artifact. Place a same-sized, wrong-hash file in the shared directory. Invoke download. The first mocked HTTP request has **no Range header**: the valid prefix was deleted. A valid candidate whose adoption is cancelled can similarly displace valuable progress.

**Impact:** merely having an unrelated same-sized model in the shared directory causes an unnecessary full re-download, directly undermining the feature's purpose and existing resume contract. With real models this can discard gigabytes of valid progress.

**Remediation:** use an independent, unique adoption staging path. Retain the previous partial and its identity until a fully verified replacement is ready to publish. On a mismatch, copy/link failure or cancellation, discard only that candidate's staging file and resume the original prefix. Test the Range offset after all these outcomes.

### R6 — Major: copy fallback bypasses disk protection and cannot be promptly cancelled

**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:382](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:382) falls back from every link exception to one awaited `copyFile`; that call has no cancellation or progress mechanism, performs no free-space check, and swallows all copy errors. `assertFreeSpace` is only reached at 847 after adoption has failed. [deployments.mjs:979](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/deployments.mjs:979) aborts and then awaits the same job, so Stop/Cancel cannot complete while copying is outstanding.

**Reproductions:**

- Force link to return EXDEV and inject a `statfs` result of zero available bytes. Adoption returns a successful copy and the space-check seam is called **zero times**. Only the tiny fixture was actually copied; this was not a disk-filling experiment.
- Hold the copy operation on a test promise, abort the signal, and observe that the operation remains unsettled. It ends with `ABORTED` only after the copy is released. No real slow/large file was needed.

**Impact:** a copy can consume the space that the download path would preserve and can hold controller Stop/Cancel/drain through a long I/O operation. A copy-space or permission failure is hidden as a candidate miss and may trigger an unnecessary network attempt.

**Remediation:** identify expected link-fallback errors, revalidate the source, and preflight the copy's actual space requirement and reserve. Copy in abortable bounded chunks (or use a managed, cancellable helper), report copying/verifying progress and clean only its own staging file. Propagate meaningful ENOSPC, cancellation and filesystem errors rather than silently treating them as a nonexistent model. Test these paths with injected faults; no large production model is needed.

### R7 — Minor: adoption provenance is missing or printed as undefined

**Evidence:** [downloader.mjs:411](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/downloader.mjs:411) returns `{source, method}`; [weightStores.mjs:103](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/weightStores.mjs:103) preserves that field; [deployments.mjs:869](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/deployments.mjs:869) prints `entry.from`. The HF store ignores `result.adopted` entirely and returns no provenance at 267–287.

**Reproduction:** real GGUF store adoption formats the controller message as `adopted model.gguf from undefined (link, verified)`. Pre-create a snapshot directory to get past R3, successfully adopt its fixture and inspect the returned object: `bytesTransferred: 0`, `adopted: undefined`.

**Impact:** DS002's promise that the deployment log names every adopted file and method is false, and acceptance evidence cannot reliably show which workspace files were reused.

**Remediation:** use one provenance shape throughout, aggregate it for every snapshot file and split shard, and test the controller's actual log output, including mixed adoption/download. Make verification a visible phase during hashing; current adoption reports ordinary download progress until the final byte and never reports copy progress.

### R8 — Minor: snapshot deletion can report zero although it removes the inode's last links

**Evidence:** [weightStores.mjs:229](/home/research/dev/local-llms/local-llm/src/controller/weightStores.mjs:229) sums only files whose current `nlink <= 1`, **before** recursively removing the whole snapshot at 293–295.

**Reproduction:** make two files inside one test snapshot hard links to the same 262,151-byte inode, with no external link. Delete that snapshot through its real store API. Both links are removed, yet `freedBytes` is zero. This topology can arise if identical pinned files were adopted from one shared inode and the operator later removed the shared pathname.

**Impact:** disk accounting understates freed content when all remaining links lie inside the deletion set. The new GGUF per-file removal does not have this particular pre-scan problem.

**Remediation:** count distinct `(device,inode)` identities and how many links the deletion set removes, or account during sequential unlinking. Do not count an inode while an external link remains. Decide whether `freedBytes` means logical content bytes or physical reclaimed blocks; the current use of `size` cannot promise exact physical space for sparse/reflinked files or files held open. Add both retained-external-link and last-internal-links tests.

## Design boundaries and plan/spec mismatches

These are not additional confirmed defects in the eight-item count:

- **Same filesystem is insufficient for a hard link in the container.** C12 says same filesystem → link. Linux returns EXDEV across different mounts even if they expose the same filesystem ([Linux link(2), EXDEV](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/link.2.html)). Ploinky separately binds the shared directory to `/shared`, while this agent declares its model store under `/data`. Therefore the normal deployed path may take the copy fallback even when a host-side operator could hard-link those same files. This is an inference from the mounts, not a container experiment. Correct the wording to “when link succeeds,” and measure link-versus-copy and peak disk in the authorized nested acceptance fixture. No Ploinky architectural change is needed merely to avoid a network download.
- **The model store is writable shared state, not immutable evidence.** R1 fixes a concrete verification bug, but stat polling cannot prevent an external write immediately after verification or while a runner reads an adopted hard link. Define whether writers are cooperative and must not alter in-use models. If the requirement is immutable bytes against concurrent writers, use an isolated verified copy/reflink or a stronger storage/snapshot mechanism; hard-linking and checking timestamps cannot provide that guarantee. Likewise, sidecar metadata stored under workspace-writable `/data` is a cache, not authentication against a writer who can also forge that metadata. Recheck the whole artifact at the last practical point before loading, especially after fetching multiple files or preparing an on-demand runner.
- **The implementation does not search the whole workspace or even every file in its own store.** It trusts only the canonical own-store path with matching verification sidecar; arbitrary-name discovery is limited to `/shared/models`. A fixture already placed at the exact canonical own-store path, with correct bytes but no sidecar, was downloaded again. DS002 explicitly narrows own-store reuse this way, so I report this as a scope/design limitation rather than a backward-compatibility defect. Consider hashing/adopting an unrecorded canonical file before downloading, and document that existing benchmark/download directories require an operator placement step. Do not move or delete the real measured files during that step without the owner's approval.
- **Snapshot digests differ from the plan's literal SHA256 wording.** C12 promises size+SHA256 for every snapshot file; DS002 and the code retain git-blob SHA1 for small Git-backed files. The fresh-snapshot fixture above used SHA256, so R3 is independent of this mismatch. Either explicitly allow the established pinned git-oid form in the plan or implement its literal SHA256 requirement. No migration requirement follows from that choice.
- **Lookup is bounded by entry count, not work or I/O volume.** Each shard/snapshot file walks the tree again and can hash many same-sized candidates. The scan has no signal checks, and each `readdir` materializes the whole directory before the 20,000-entry cap is applied. A large cache should use a cancellable streaming walk or an advisory size/hash index whose candidates are still verified. This is an unmeasured scaling concern, not a claim that this review observed a large-cache failure.
- **The owner's model-retention instruction remains in force.** Product tests may remove their disposable fixtures; engineering must keep the real downloaded models. None of these findings calls for deleting a real model or reclaiming disk as a workaround.

## Verification and missing tests

From the immutable snapshot I ran:

```sh
node --test local-llm/tests/shared-models.test.mjs \
  local-llm/tests/downloader.test.mjs \
  local-llm/tests/hf-snapshot.test.mjs \

  local-llm/tests/controller.test.mjs
```

**Result: 71 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.** The implementation log's full-suite `301/301` is a reported engineering result; I did not independently rerun the whole suite. The six new tests in `shared-models.test.mjs` use single GGUF files and do not cover a real controller Run, a fresh adopted HF snapshot, or split-file adoption. Their static symlink and between-call mutation fixtures do not cover R1/R2. The old-record test is permissible, but preserving old record behavior is not an acceptance requirement.

The additional isolated script below ran successfully and confirmed 12 observations: R1; both R2 paths; R3; R4; R5; both R6 paths; both R7 paths; R8; and the unrecorded-own-file design limitation. Test hooks only schedule races, simulate EXDEV/space and hold a copy; they do not alter the reviewed implementation. No GPU or network is used.

After fixes, add the above regression cases and an end-to-end **small fixture** matrix: complete, incomplete, corrupt and mixed-source split GGUF/HF snapshots; completion only after every required file verifies; partial preservation; Stop/Cancel/drain; actual provenance; and inode-aware deletion. Then the authorized Spark acceptance can prove model reuse with the already-retained pinned weights. Correct bytes and zero network transfer must be demonstrated independently from runner performance.

## Reproduction appendix

The preserved script is also at `/tmp/c12-review-ywenp317/reproduce_codex.mjs`. To reproduce against the exact commit in a separate small source copy:

**12. Reuse weights that already exist in the workspace** (owner, 2026-09-28; §9, item 6). Phase 2.

- **Where to look.** Before any download, the controller looks for the pinned artifact:
  - in its own store (`/data/models`, as today);
  - in the workspace's shared directory `/shared/models/`, which is `<workspace>/.data/shared/models` on the host and is mounted into every agent. An operator can place files there, for example by hard-linking them from another workspace or from a download directory on the same filesystem.

  Inside the Box, manifest volumes must stay inside the workspace, so the agent cannot see host directories outside it.

C12 is revised after Codex's review. The plan is now sha256 738778a029ef7dc88b384126e29bb07e3be2bb175f1cb0e391512eaa42d11e8d.

The authoritative text is in the plan: C12, and §9 item 8 (which maps each finding to its class, the C12 section and the test numbers). The full review, with its reproduction appendix, is plans/local-llm-workspace-reuse-review_codex.md. Source, the specs and the tests stay yours. The summary follows.

TRUST MODEL (this settles R1, R2 and link vs copy):
- /data is written only by the agent and the operator, and is trusted at that level. Its records are a cache, not authentication.
- /shared is read-write for every agent, so its contents are untrusted input.
- Hashing proves only the bytes it read. Stat checks afterwards detect accidents; they do not guarantee immutability.
- Nothing from /shared is ever hard-linked. Inside the container, /shared and /data are separate mounts, so link() returns EXDEV anyway.

LOOKUP ORDER:
1. The agent's own store, as today.
2. In-place adoption (new; the zero-copy path). A regular file at the canonical store path, of the pinned size, with no valid record, is hashed and adopted where it is. The operator puts it there by hard-linking into <ws>/.data/local-llm/models/... on the host. DS002 documents the canonical paths. Warn in the log when the adopted file has other links.
3. /shared/models: a private copy only, hashed while it is written.
4. Otherwise download or resume.

MATCHING: the exact size plus the pinned digest (sha256, or the pinned git blob id, as in DS002) of every file, shard and snapshot file. Names only order candidates.

R1 and R2, binding verification to the bytes hashed:
- Open with O_NOFOLLOW and require a regular file.
- Confirm through readlink /proc/self/fd/N that the opened file is under the allowed root. This covers swapped ancestors. Fail closed if you can't.
- Hash through that fd, with an identical fstat before and after.
- Record the identity of the hashed object, allowing for the ctime change from your own rename.
- Never take identity from a symlink. A symlink anywhere in the store is treated as absent and logged.

R5: a unique staging file per candidate. Leave .partial and its identity record untouched until a verified replacement is published. On a mismatch, error or abort, remove only the staging file, and resume from the earlier offset.

R6: a copy follows the download's rules:
- check free space for the file plus the reserve before starting;
- copy in abortable chunks, so Stop, Cancel and drain settle within one chunk;
- report copying and verifying progress;
- surface ENOSPC and other I/O errors as errors, never as "no candidate".

R4: the disk term of admission comes from the acquisition plan:
- 0 for files already owned or adoptable in place;
- full size plus the reserve for a copy (a change from your current in-progress assumption, since links from /shared are gone);
- the remaining bytes for a download.
Run, preview and overview must agree. Memory and GPU refusal still come first. DS003 covers this.

R3: create the final and staging directories under the store root, rejecting symlinked ancestors, before adopting.

R7: one provenance shape for every file and shard: {file, source, method: in-place | copy | download, bytes}. Show it in the log and the results. Hashing appears as the verifying phase.

R8: freedBytes is the logical size of each distinct (dev, ino) whose last link the deletion removed. An inode that still has a link outside the deletion set counts 0.

ALSO:
- Just before the runner starts, stat-check every file of the artifact, and re-hash any whose identity changed.
- Lookup is one streaming, cancellable walk per artifact. Hash at most 3 same-size candidates per file, name matches first.

TESTS: C12 lists 14 desired-behaviour regression tests, converted from Codex's appendix. Use small disposable fixtures only: no GPU, no network, and never the real models.

ACCEPTANCE (Spark, after the matrix):
- Hard-link the retained gpt-oss-20b into the test workspace's canonical store path. Run must adopt it in place with 0 network bytes and a matching sha256.
- A small pinned model placed in .data/shared/models must be copied and verified. Record the time and peak disk use.
- The real models are only linked and read, per the owner's retention rule.

Codex will independently verify your fixes.

**The trust model for files other agents can write** (C12, "Trust model"):
- **`/data`, the agent's own store:** only the agent and the operator write to it, so it's trusted at operator level. Its record files are a cache, not authentication.
- **`/shared`:** every agent in the workspace can write to it, so everything there is untrusted input.
- **What checks prove:** hashing proves only the bytes that were actually read. Later stat and timestamp checks only catch accidental changes. The plan says explicitly that they don't guarantee the file can't change.

**Resulting design:**
- **No hard links from `/shared`:** its files are only copied privately and hashed while being copied. This goes further than your "when link succeeds" wording, for two reasons:
  - a link would let every agent write to the adopted file;
  - `/data` and `/shared` are separate mounts in the container, so `link()` fails with EXDEV there anyway.
- **Zero-copy reuse is in-place adoption:** the operator hard-links a file into the agent's own store at its expected path, and the agent verifies it there.

**Finding-to-action mapping** (full table in plan §9 item 8; test numbers refer to C12's list):

| Finding | Class | Action in C12 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 hash-then-stat race | Implementation fix; contract clarified | Hash through an opened file handle, with identical stat before and after; record the object that was hashed, allowing for our own rename (tests 2, 14) |
| R2 symlink and ancestor escape | Implementation fix (already required); scope extended | Open without following symlinks; confirm through `/proc/self/fd` that the file is inside the allowed directory, or fail closed; no symlinks anywhere in the store (tests 3, 9) |
| R3 fresh-snapshot ENOENT | Implementation fix | Create the destination and staging directories safely before adopting (test 1) |
| R4 disk check before reuse | Changed contract | Disk admission counts bytes actually needed: 0 for in-place or owned files, full size plus reserve for a copy, remaining bytes for a download. Run and previews agree (tests 5, 6) |
| R5 partial destroyed | Implementation fix; staging made explicit | Each candidate gets its own staging file; the existing partial stays untouched until a verified replacement is ready (tests 4, 10) |
| R6 copy fallback | Implementation fix; made explicit | Copies follow the download's rules: space check, cancellable chunks, progress, real errors reported (tests 5, 10) |
| R7 provenance | Implementation fix | One provenance record for every file, shard and snapshot file; hashing shown as the verifying phase (test 8) |
| R8 freed bytes | Implementation fix; definition explicit | Count an inode's size only when the deletion removes its last link (test 11) |
| Links fail across mounts (EXDEV) | Changed contract | Copy only from `/shared` |
| Writers and immutability | Changed contract | Explicit trust model, plus a stat check of every file just before the runner starts, with re-hash on change (test 14) |
| Unrecorded file at the expected path | Changed contract | In-place adoption (tests 6, 7) |
| sha256 vs git blob ids | Plan wording fix | "The pinned digest", matching DS002 (test 1) |
| Scan cost | Changed contract | One cancellable walk per model; at most 3 same-size candidates hashed per file (test 13) |
| Model retention | Unchanged | Tests use throwaway fixtures; real models are only linked and read |

- a retained model hard-linked into the store is adopted in place with zero network bytes and a matching sha256;
- a small model placed in `.data/shared/models` is copied and verified, with time and peak disk recorded.
